Tools from my lab's methods work, alongside the data and code behind individual
papers.

## R packages

### metameta

Calculates and visualises study-level statistical power in meta-analyses across a
range of hypothetical effect sizes. It can be used to reanalyse published
meta-analyses from standard forest plot information, or applied to a new one.
Key functions are `mapower_se()` and `mapower_ul()` for power estimates, and
`firepower()` for plots comparing median power across several meta-analyses.

```r
devtools::install_github("dsquintana/metameta")
```

[GitHub](https://github.com/dsquintana/metameta) ·
[Web app](https://dsquintana.shinyapps.io/metameta_app/) ·
[Paper](https://doi.org/10.1177/25152459221147260)

### ESDist

Calculates and visualises field-specific effect size distributions from data
extracted from meta-analyses, so that empirical benchmarks can replace generic
rules of thumb. Includes publication-bias-adjusted variants, and `esd_perc()` for
locating a given effect within its field's distribution. Written by
[Bernt Glaser](https://github.com/berntgl); I'm a co-author on the accompanying
tutorial.

```r
devtools::install_github("berntgl/ESDist")
```

[GitHub](https://github.com/berntgl/ESDist) ·
[Paper](https://doi.org/10.3758/s13428-026-03003-2)

## Data and code

Data, analysis scripts, and preregistrations for individual papers are linked
directly from each entry on the [Publications](publications.qmd) page, so they sit
next to the study they belong to rather than in a separate index. Most live on
[OSF](https://osf.io/user/8e3md); some are on
[GitHub](https://github.com/dsquintana).
